messages.subject: About thermoregulatory behavior in Fortran
parts:
Hi all,

I am a bit confused about how thermoregulation is controlled in the Fortran code, which is probaby related to my little Fortran knowledge.

The point is that it seems to me that thermoregulatory adjustments are coded both in the ECTOTHERM.f and THERMO.f subroutines. So, if I wanted to include different regulatory responses, should I modify both files?

Thank you very much!

Best,
Urtzi

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: About thermoregulatory behavior in Fortran
parts:
Hi Urtzi,

Yes it's a bit of a complicated beast and there are indeed bits in THERMO.f and ECTOTHERM.f. I will probably make a more modularised version of it at some point like I have done for the endotherm model. Points for bravery in trying to adapt it!

All the best,
Mike

Hi Mike,

Thank you so much! For now I am just learning, so I want to make simple modifications. I was thinking on adding an additional step before putting the animal (a newt in this case) aboveground. The idea is to check whether environmental conditions aboveground are aproppriate in terms of water balance before cheking for temperature, and put the animal in the burrow if too "dry". Let's see how it goes!

All the best,
Urtzi
